rules.name: Prerequisite Courses (Part 1)
rules.notes: Must be taken for a letter grade, and for 4-5 units. Strongly recommended to be taken before the winter quarter of the junior year.

rules.name: Prerequisite Courses (Part 2)
rules.notes: Must be taken for a letter grade, and for 4-5 units. Strongly recommended to be taken before the winter quarter of the junior year.

rules.name: Elective/Specialization Courses

children.name: Two or three 100-level undergraduate courses (8 units)
Elective choices approved by the Student Services Administrator

rules.desc:
Elective/Specialization Courses
Two or three university-wide undergraduate courses at the 100-level, totaling a minimum of 8 units. These courses must be taken for a letter grade, and be a minimum of 3 units each.
Electives/specialization courses are designed to support research conducted for or connected to the student’s honors thesis topic.
Specialization courses can be completed anytime, and courses taken before acceptance into the program can be used to fulfill this requirement. These course choices must be reviewed and approved for counting towards the Honors Program with the Student Services Administrator. Syllabi/relevant coursework may be requested for this review process.

rules.name: EiS Program Specific Coursework
rules.desc:
ETHICSOC190 is a mandatory seminar for juniors who are accepted into the honors program. This seminar is only offered during winter quarter and must be attended in person.
ETHICSOC195 is a mandatory one-unit writing workshop that must be taken in the winter quarter of senior year.
During the senior year of the honors program, students enroll in graded thesis writing units (200A-C) that can vary between 3-5 units per quarter, and should total to a minimum of 10 units over the course of the senior year. Students will enroll in ETHICSOC 200A in the fall quarter, ETHICSOC 200B in the winter quarter, and ETHICSOC 200C in the spring quarter.

grading: All required courses for the program must be taken for a letter grade
policies: EiS Program Specific Courses cannot be double-counted between the Ethics in Society Honors Program and other academic programs.
transferPolicy: Students hoping to apply transfer credit and/or courses taken abroad towards the honors program must request approval with the student services administrator. Syllabi/relevant coursework may be requested for this review process.
reviewNotes: Every course must be letter graded. You take one political philosophy and one moral philosophy course of 4-5 units, two or three 100-level undergraduate courses of at least 3 units totaling 8 units that the Student Services Administrator approves, ETHICSOC 190 and 195, and ETHICSOC 200A, 200B and 200C totaling at least 10 units. Your advisor checks that the program's own courses are not also counted toward another program, and any transfer or abroad courses.
